name: Buckinghamshire
description: Buckinghamshire is a largely rural and affluent county north-west of London, characterised by rolling Chiltern countryside, historic villages and market towns. It includes places such as Aylesbury, High Wycombe and Milton Keynes, with strong transport and economic links to London.

places.name: Aylesbury Vale
places.description: A rural district in Buckinghamshire named for the fertile Vale of Aylesbury, home to the county town of Aylesbury and close to Waddesdon Manor, a lavish Rothschild estate.

places.name: Chiltern
places.description: A former district in Buckinghamshire covering the Chiltern Hills' beech woodlands and the towns of Amersham and Chesham.

places.name: Milton Keynes
places.description: A planned New Town in Buckinghamshire built from 1967, known for its grid-system roads, extensive parkland, and iconic concrete cow sculptures.

places.name: South Bucks
places.description: A former affluent, rural district in Buckinghamshire near the Thames, covering villages close to Slough and Burnham Beeches ancient woodland.

places.name: Wycombe
places.description: A former district in Buckinghamshire centred on High Wycombe, historically the centre of England's furniture-making industry, particularly Windsor chairs.
